items.title: 67802_Charles Mingus oral history interview
items.q: I think George Wain had time on the program, but he still wouldn't play any jazz records.

ctx.x: Yeah, you mentioned Nat Hentoff in your -- said he was -- when you were in New York, he was one of the people who gave you -- wrote a lot about you and said good things about you.

No, in my book, I said -- I got him concerned in jazz. I met him when he was a classical disc jockey in Boston. And I think George Wain had time on the program, but he still wouldn't play any jazz records. I got him into jazz.

I'm pretty sure he'll tell you that. He played only classical -- at home he might have some jazz records, I don't know about that, but it appeared to me that he didn't know anything about jazz. I used to write letters to him. There's A (dable) letter I wrote to him describing what a bass violin will be doing ten years from the time I wrote the letter. And it's just what they're doing right now. Broken lines, broken rhythms.
